title: Firefighter Academy
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

outcomes: Identify minimum qualifications and entry skills needed for fire service-related jobs.

Demonstrate the ability to analyze, appraise, and evaluate key firefighting tactics including size-up procedures, the incident command system, adherence to the ten standard fire orders, and the 18 situations that shout watch out.
Compare and contrast the behavior of fire in enclosed versus open environments, including the various phases of fire development in buildings.
Describe application and limits of tools and equipment used in fire suppression.

notes: The catalog prints codes without a space (KIN13, FT185, FT187); these match closed-list KIN 13, FT 185, and FT 187.
The catalog lists FT185 at 14 credits; the state file stores FT 185 at 13.5 units. The catalog value (14) was recorded.
The catalog counts the award in credits (semester units); the total of 18 credits is stated.

The careers entry is taken from the description, which says the certificate prepares students for 'the roles and responsibilities of a Firefighter recruit or for entry-level employment'. 'Entry-level employment' and employment 'at fire departments' are not named job titles, so they were not recorded.
